Established in 1957, IMV CORPORATION specializes in environmental testing,measurement and analysis equipment for vibration-related applications. We are also proud of our test systems, which are used in automotive & aerospace applications and for a variety of other industrial products to help maintain the high quality and reliability for which Japanese technology is famous. 
In addition to standard vibration test systems, we also produce specialized, all-weather systems capable of testing vibration in a wide variety of temperature and humidity conditions, and multi-degree of freedom test system which can reproduce more realistic field vibration. Currently, we expand our business area into battery testing, and receive high evaluations in those developings. In recent years, we have evolved beyond the framework of a typical manufacturer to focus on internationally-respected testing and solutions services.In the measurement systems field, we offer seismic monitoring systems, large-scale vibration monitoring systems, portable vibration systems and a wide range of other products.

entityDescription:
Electrek Explorer is an innovative software and data platform designed to transform electric mobility and travel by integrating nature-focused geospatial data with advanced mapping and navigation systems. The platform curates and analyzes environmental, ecological, and experiential data to enable businesses, organisations, and travelers to access alternate route guidance and curated experiences that emphasize sustainability, biodiversity, and natural exploration.
At its core, Electrek Explorer offers a suite of geospatial data and APIs that can be integrated into third-party platforms to enhance electric mobility and outdoor travel experiences. Through its "Explorer Route" feature, the platform enables users to discover scenic, eco-friendly routes while connecting with local conservation projects and biodiversity hotspots.
Key functionalities include:
Alternate Route Guidance: Integration of curated nature-focused routes into mapping systems for electric vehicles, bikes, and other modes of sustainable transport.

Geospatial Data Solutions: Providing comprehensive datasets for outdoor experiences, including eco-friendly charging points, wildlife observation areas, and protected natural reserves.

Platform Integration: Seamless integration into existing mobility, navigation, and tourism platforms to enhance user engagement and promote sustainable exploration.

By fostering deeper connections between technology, mobility, and nature, Electrek Explorer aims to create meaningful travel experiences, support conservation efforts, and encourage responsible exploration of interconnected ecosystems.

description:
CeraNovis produces, applies and develops ceramic coatings for harsh environments. One of the application fields, are thermo-optical coatings for satellite surfaces
 This white ceramic coating (calles NV14) has been developed within the framework of the ESA’s Bepi Colombo Mission. The task was to develop a white, UV-resistant reflecting coating that is particularly inert to thermal shocks. Currently, this flexible coating can be applied to substrates such as titanium, titanium foils, steel, CFRP and aluminum. It withstands temperature changes of -200°C to +500°C. I can be thermally sintered but simple drying under ambient conditions is also sufficient. Due to the low sintering temperatures the substrate properties remain unchanged. The ageing resistance of the coating has been determined by simulation tests under high vacuum, high temperature and high UV load (11 solar constants) over several years. CeraNovis offers the complete coating of components, also with complex geometries.. Upon request we offer documentation in the form of a CoT (Certificate of Test) with microscopic investigation, tape tests and process control samples.

entityDescription: The Aerospace Mechatronics Group is a research unit at the University of Toronto Institute for Aerospace Studies (UTIAS) in Toronto, Canada, under the supervision of Prof. M. Reza Emami. He was also the Founding Chaired Professor of Onboard Space Systems and Director of Asteroid Engineering Centre at the Luleå University of Technology, Sweden, in 2015-2020. He obtained his Ph.D. and postdoctoral fellowship in Robotics and Mechatronics from University of Toronto, and M.A.Sc. and B.Sc. in Aerospace Engineering from Sharif University of Technology, and worked in the industry as a licensed Professional Engineer and Project Manager before joining the academia. His research focuses on concurrent engineering of multidisciplinary systems, such as spacecraft, robot manipulators and rovers. Some of his current research includes: space systems miniaturization, space debris mitigation and remediation, concurrent base-arm control of free-flying space manipulators, satellite formation flying, asteroid redirection for exploration and mining, intelligent heterogeneous rover/satellite teams, and reconfigurable manipulators. Prof. Emami is the Associate Editor of Frontiers in Space Technologies and International Journal of Advanced Robotic Systems, Guest Editor of MDPI’s Journal of Aerospace, and Honorary Rosalind Member of London Journals Press. He has been nominated for several awards, including National Innovation for Technology Award and OPAS Award for Excellence in Teaching. He was also recognized by MathWorks as a Featured Professor in 2013 and 2003, and was in the list of University of Toronto's Miracle Workers in 2000.

entityDescription:
The Nature Research Centre(NRC)is a state research institute conducting scientific research and experimental development in the field of natural sciences.
Vision
The NRC is an internationally competitive higher education and research institution conducting fundamental and applied research on living and non-living nature, which helps ensuring the quality and continuity of the life of society in conditions of diverse changes in ecosystems and emerging social challenges.
Mission
The mission of the NRC is to develop fundamental and applied research by accumulating, summarizing and disseminating new knowledge in the field of natural sciences, which is necessary for ensuring the knowledge and protection of ecosystems and sustainable use of resources to meet the needs of society.
Activity objectives
- To carry out long-term research and experimental (social, cultural) development in ecology, botany, mycology, microbiology, virology, zoology, parasitology and geosciences relevant for the continuity and development of the country’s economy, culture, health care and society.
- To cooperate with representatives of business, government and society, to carry out contracted research and experimental (social, cultural) development, and to provide methodological support related to the creation and use of methods and other assistance.
- To raise public awareness of scientific knowledge, to use it in culture, education, health care, as well as social and economic activities, to contribute to the creation of economy based on innovation and knowledge and to the development of knowledge-intensive society.

entityDescription:
ICEE Space is an international space test-, research- and development startup specialising in empowering and operating analogue missions for high-fidelity simulation of crewed and robotic space missions.

We provide cutting-edge technology such as ready-to-use mobile inflatable habitats and analogue space suits, infrastructure to set up research test-beds in extreme environments on Earth, as well as analogue consultancy services. Our goal is to aid future interplanetary exploration on the Moon, Mars, and beyond, as analogue research is key to unlocking deep space research.

Our product is our analogue astronaut toolkit, comprising an inflatable habitat, analogue spacesuits, communication systems, power systems, MCC procedure and guidelines, mission design and research methodologies, training suits, and environment monitoring software. The kit provides everything an aspiring space researcher might need to design and run an analogue mission, anywhere in the world. It allows various research groups to organise scientific expeditions with high science returns in human performance, human-robotic interactions, and AI in extreme environments, while also promoting high and uniform industry standards.

Additionally, we also provide analogue consulting services and run analogue expeditions, with 4 already under our belt.
In 2021, our team had the first campaign in the lava tube of Stefánshellir, Iceland. This and subsequent ICEE.Space missions (CHILL-ICE II, APICES, CASTHELS) serve as test-beds for our astronaut toolkit and help refine our expertise. Our next analogue mission, CHILL-ICE III, is planned for August of 2024.

We are backed by ESA BIC, the biggest network of incubators supporting European space startups.

entityDescription:
Medical University - Plovdiv
The Medical University of Plovdiv (MU-Plovdiv) is a state-accredited institution, founded in 1945, with over 37,700 alumni from 65 countries across Europe, Asia, America, and Africa. As a member of the European University Association, MU-Plovdiv holds the prestigious Erasmus University Charter, allowing participation in EU educational programs. This ensures high-quality education, alongside mobility opportunities for both students and faculty members. The university's educational activities are also certified under ISO 9001:2015.
MU-Plovdiv is comprised of four faculties: Medicine, Dental Medicine, Pharmacy, and Public Health. It also includes a Medical College and a Department of Languages and Specialized Training. The university aligns its curricula with other European institutions, promoting the European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System (ECTS). This system facilitates the mutual recognition of qualifications and encourages student mobility. Clinical training is carried out at six affiliated university hospitals. Since 2007, MU-Plovdiv diplomas have been recognized by all EU and EEA member countries.
The academic staff includes over 200 professors and associate professors, as well as 600 assistant professors. These professionals are known for their significant scientific achievements and extensive teaching experience. Many are active members of international research teams and organizations, contributing to advancements in medical science and education.
Research at MU-Plovdiv is overseen by the Vice-Rector of Science and Research, supported by the Council of Science and Research, as well as other experts and auxiliary units. The university offers nearly 70 doctoral programs spanning medicine, dental medicine, pharmacy, public health, and the natural sciences.
The research community at MU-Plovdiv benefits from advanced research and innovation centers that foster interdisciplinary collaboration. These centers are equipped with cutting-edge technologies, promoting both basic and clinical research, with a strong focus on translating scientific findings into clinical practice. The recently renovated Vivarium provides additional facilities for experimental and preclinical research. Research findings are often disseminated through MU-Plovdiv's academic journal, Folia Medica, which is indexed in Scopus. The university also supports young researchers through the Youth Scientific Association, encouraging their involvement in research projects and scientific events.
MU-Plovdiv's international relations are managed by the International Relations and Foreign Students Department. The university has signed over 150 academic agreements, including Erasmus+ inter-institutional agreements with universities across the EU and beyond. It is also a member of over 15 international academic organizations, offering diverse exchange opportunities through programs such as Erasmus+, CEEPUS, OMI, and Fulbright.
The Department of Medical Physics and Biophysics at MU-Plovdiv upholds the university’s high academic and research standards. The department's research focuses on a variety of experimental animal models, including in vivo, in vitro, and ex vivo studies. Research includes preclinical testing of newly synthesized biologically active molecules, the development of new drug delivery systems, biophysical experiments investigating cell pathways using isolated smooth muscle samples, and cytotoxic studies on primary cell cultures using a real-time cell analyzer. In recent years, the department has embarked on microgravitational studies using rats and mice. To support this research, part of the team developed a modified random positioning machine, suitable for both in vivo and in vitro experiments.

MU-Plovdiv is comprised of four faculties: Medicine, Dental Medicine, Pharmacy, and Public Health. It also includes a Medical College and a Department of Languages and Specialized Training. The university aligns its curricula with other European institutions, promoting the European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System (ECTS). This system facilitates the mutual recognition of qualifications and encourages student mobility. Clinical training is carried out at six affiliated university hospitals. Since 2007, MU-Plovdiv diplomas have been recognized by all EU and EEA member countries.
The academic staff includes over 200 professors and associate professors, as well as 600 assistant professors. These professionals are known for their significant scientific achievements and extensive teaching experience. Many are active members of international research teams and organizations, contributing to advancements in medical science and education.
Research at MU-Plovdiv is overseen by the Vice-Rector of Science and Research, supported by the Council of Science and Research, as well as other experts and auxiliary units. The university offers nearly 70 doctoral programs spanning medicine, dental medicine, pharmacy, public health, and the natural sciences.
The research community at MU-Plovdiv benefits from advanced research and innovation centers that foster interdisciplinary collaboration. These centers are equipped with cutting-edge technologies, promoting both basic and clinical research, with a strong focus on translating scientific findings into clinical practice. The recently renovated Vivarium provides additional facilities for experimental and preclinical research. Research findings are often disseminated through MU-Plovdiv's academic journal, Folia Medica, which is indexed in Scopus. The university also supports young researchers through the Youth Scientific Association, encouraging their involvement in research projects and scientific events.
MU-Plovdiv's international relations are managed by the International Relations and Foreign Students Department. The university has signed over 150 academic agreements, including Erasmus+ inter-institutional agreements with universities across the EU and beyond. It is also a member of over 15 international academic organizations, offering diverse exchange opportunities through programs such as Erasmus+, CEEPUS, OMI, and Fulbright.
The Department of Medical Physics and Biophysics at MU-Plovdiv upholds the university’s high academic and research standards. The department's research focuses on a variety of experimental animal models, including in vivo, in vitro, and ex vivo studies. Research includes preclinical testing of newly synthesized biologically active molecules, the development of new drug delivery systems, biophysical experiments investigating cell pathways using isolated smooth muscle samples, and cytotoxic studies on primary cell cultures using a real-time cell analyzer. In recent years, the department has embarked on microgravitational studies using rats and mice. To support this research, part of the team developed a modified random positioning machine, suitable for both in vivo and in vitro experiments.

description: Maana Electric SA was founded in 2018 in Luxembourg with the aim to develop proprietary In-Situ Resources Utilization (ISRU) technologies for the extraction of resources from low-value feedstock (i.e., desert sand and planetary regolith). Company description: As a partner for digitization, Industry 4.0 and the Internet of Things, the Fraunhofer Institute for Applied Information Technology FIT has been developing IT solutions tailored to people and seamlessly integrated into business processes for 40 years. As a driving force of innovation, FIT not only provides guidance, but also shapes the digital transformation in business, the environment and society.

Each of FIT's informatics departments is built around one of our five core competencies:

- Data Science & Artificial Intelligencedrives the digital transformation by processing, organizing and analyzing data and knowledge more systematically and flexibly than before. Our senior scientists have internationally renowned expertise in process mining and semantic data integration;
- Cooperation Systemsfocuses on a research field that has been a mainstay of Fraunhofer FIT: Collaboration and the cooperative use of distributed data or services on different levels – for example, using Mixed Reality or Blockchain technology;
- Microsimulation & Econometric Data Analysiswill continue to provide the German federal government with evidence-based predictions on the impact of political decisions, such as tax revenue forecasts that take demographic change into account;
- Information Systems Engineeringexplores the use of digital technologies in business organizations via software and hardware demonstrators, assists with the selection and implementation of complex enterprise software, and develops concepts for management issues in the IT environment.

entityDescription:
MetaPlanet's aim is to make the vast amount of data about the Earth collected from space available to the general public in an unprecedentedly simple way.

The company's objective is to develop a basic artificial intelligence model for Earth observation that uses time series of high-resolution satellite images to construct a 4D (space and time) representation of the planet with a high level of detail, using techniques such as super-resolution, generative AI and monocular depth estimation.

The AI system consists of two parts: MetaPlanet and AI Analytics. MetaPlanet is a generic AI model and machine representation of the world (different from the usual digital twins), optimised to be queried by other AI agents. An LLM can connect to MetaPlanet. MetaPlanet will thus become an exploitable source of information for all companies and individuals outside the space sector.

entityDescription:
We are an entity focused on raising social awareness through video games, with specialized expertise in Virtual Reality (VR) and a patented approach to visual neuro-rehabilitation using VR. Our team has deep knowledge in Artificial Intelligence, particularly in autoregressive models, autoencoders, 3D reconstruction, and large language models (LLMs).
Currently, we are engaged in multiple European projects under the Horizon Europe Programme, collaborating with special education schools to support children with special needs. Our work spans a range of multidisciplinary projects, including video game design (from AAA titles to simplified or cartoon-style environments for users with visual and cognitive impairments), as well as the development of analytical tools, web interfaces, and performance reporting systems.
We have extensive experience in facilitating collaboration among diverse teams, bridging the gap between ICT experts and professionals from various fields such as special education, clinical psychology, neuropsychology, and occupational therapy among others.
